title: Three for One: Philly Consolidates, JMoney Restocks, and the Model Says Nobody Wins
dek: Alan sent Isaiah Likely, Emeka Egbuka, and Denzel Boston to Jordan for Ashton Jeanty, and the math left Team Pillbert lighter on title odds than it was before the call.
body: The ledger finally got its own write-up. Before Week 5, Alan's Team Pillbert shipped tight end Isaiah Likely and wide receivers Emeka Egbuka and Denzel Boston to Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV for running back Ashton Jeanty. It's a classic three-for-one, quantity for quality, between a 3-1 contender and a team sitting at 0-4. The scoring math is the funny part: the three players Jordan received had combined for 64.8 points before the deal, and Jeanty alone had 64.4.

Start with what JMoney got, because on raw totals he came out 0.4 points ahead. Egbuka is the headliner with 28.6 points over four weeks on a roster, about 7.2 a week. Boston had 18 points in just two weeks, a 9-a-week pace that's the most interesting rate in the package, and Likely added 18.2 over three weeks, roughly 6.1 a week. That's three bodies for a roster that has needed help, and after Garrett Wilson's 4.2 last week, a deeper receiver room isn't a bad thing to own.

Alan's side is the concentrated bet. Jeanty had 64.4 points across four weeks, a steady 16.1 a week, which is more than double the weekly rate of any single player he gave up. The logic is the same one every contender eventually reaches: lineup spots are limited, and one guy scoring 16 is worth more than three guys scoring 6 to 9 who can't all start. Philly has been aggressive all month, and this was another swing at turning depth into firepower.

Then came the verdict, and it wasn't kind to Philly. Team Pillbert's title odds dropped from 21% to 16%, a 5-point hit on a deal Alan initiated. Counting or not Counting GV went from 0% to 0%, which is the model's polite way of saying Jordan's season wasn't going to be rescued by any trade. On paper, that makes Jordan the winner by default: he lost nothing, gained 0.4 points of past production, and walked away with three roster pieces. Alan paid five points of title odds for the privilege of consolidating.

The context makes this one even stranger, since the trade ledger shows Jeanty didn't stay long in Pillbert colors, heading to Mekhi in the deal that brought Justin Jefferson to Alan. So the real test of this trade is whether Egbuka, Boston, and Likely can give JMoney a win against Zoe in Week 5 and keep him off 0-5. If they can, the receiver haul will look like the start of a rebuild. If not, the only scoreboard where Jordan won this deal is the one that counts points scored before it happened.

social.author: GV Faithful
social.text: We gave up 64.4 points. We got back 64.8 points. Plus three players. Plus odds held perfectly steady. Undefeated in trades, winless in games. One of those is about to change.

social.author: Pillbert Nation
social.text: Three guys out, one RB in, odds 21% to 16%. The model doesn't understand roster spots. We do. Trust the process, it has a lot of steps.

social.author: The Spreadsheet Sage
social.text: Weekly rates: Jeanty 16.1, Boston 9.0, Egbuka 7.2, Likely 6.1. Philly bought the best player. The model charged him five percentage points for it anyway.

social.author: Buckaroo Insider
social.text: Sources say Philly's phone has more trade notifications this month than JMoney has wins. Sources also say Jeanty's moving boxes never got unpacked.

social.author: Zilgit's Web
social.text: Cute haul, Counting or not Counting GV. Egbuka, Boston, Likely, all debuting against us in Week 5. Bundle up, it gets cold up here.
